educationActivity.maintext:
# Educational Activity of the College

The Agrotechnical College delivers secondary professional and additional education programs. The learning process is based on national standards, modern teaching methods, and a practice‑oriented approach.

## Key Areas

- Training qualified specialists in the college’s priority fields
- Practical learning in laboratories, training sites, and partner organizations
- Student participation in projects, olympiads, competitions, and conferences
- Support for employment and career development of graduates

## Learning Process

1. Theoretical training with up‑to‑date learning materials
2. Practical classes and internships
3. Interim and final assessment according to established requirements

## Quality and Development

The college continuously improves its programs, updates methodological materials, and strengthens its technical base. We work with employers so graduates gain relevant skills and are competitive in the job market.

## Student Support

- Teacher and curator consultations
- Methodological support for projects and internships
- Additional courses and workshops

cooperation.maintext:
## Open to the World

The Sultan Ibraimov Agrotechnical College is a leader in vocational education in Kyrgyzstan and is actively integrating into the international educational space. It was one of the first colleges to establish partnerships with foreign organizations, enabling the modernization of the learning environment and the implementation of international educational standards.

## Key Areas of International Cooperation

### Educational Programs and Projects

- **Germany (2006)** – In collaboration with the Weihenstephan University of Applied Sciences, a program in "Entrepreneurship in Agriculture" was developed according to European standards.
- **Finland (since 2014)** – The University of Eastern Finland supports the development of ichthyology and fish farming. The college has established an Aquaculture Center, a water laboratory, and a training fish farm, developed courses, and trained teachers.
- **Japan (since 2018)** – Cooperation with the Agricultural School of Shihoro (JICA). New products based on local resources (e.g., sea buckthorn oatmeal cookies) have been developed, and practical agricultural education programs have been improved. In 2023, a Memorandum was signed with Iwatani School in Japan for student exchange and academic cooperation.
- **Kazakhstan (2023)** – A Memorandum with Ushkonur College on joint training of specialists in dual education.

### Infrastructure Projects

- **USA (2003-2005)** – The American Mercy Corps helped equip the college with furniture and educational equipment.
- **OSCE (2011)** – "Water Quality in Kyrgyzstan" project, under which the college received a mobile chemical laboratory from the Japanese Embassy.
- **Asia (2015-2018)** – The Asian Development Bank’s "Vocational Education" project. The college established modern laboratories for "Hydrotechnical Construction" and "Veterinary" specialties.
- **Saudi Arabia (2023)** – Participation in a project to improve vocational education infrastructure, including major repairs and laboratory equipment.

## The Future of International Cooperation

The college continues to expand international ties, implement innovative educational methodologies, and improve infrastructure, opening new opportunities for students.

✨ The journey of discovery continues…

titles.seven: LAND RECLAMATION, REHABILITATION, AND SOIL PROTECTION

descriptions.two:
AGRONOMIST is one of the oldest professions.

The agronomist is the main conductor of science in agriculture, defining farming technology and how work is organized.

Today agronomists are in demand at large agricultural enterprises as well as small farms, orangeries, nurseries and greenhouses.

The AGRONOMIST is one of the key figures in the countryside. Their main task is to improve agricultural production and manage the work of machine operators, field workers and other staff. Advantages of the profession: varied work, usefulness and importance to society.
descriptions.three:
VETERINARY SCIENCE literally means caring for and treating livestock. It is a field of scientific knowledge and practical work aimed at fighting animal diseases, protecting people from infections common to animals and humans, producing sanitary-safe products and solving veterinary and sanitary problems of environmental protection.
In the Kyrgyz Republic, livestock farming is one of the main branches of agriculture. The efficiency and volume of its output depend largely on veterinary services.
Broad training allows graduates to apply their knowledge both in the agro-industrial complex and in other sectors of the country's economy.
descriptions.four:
Kyrgyzstan is a mountainous country, and its rivers are the main source for developing irrigation and energy.

HYDRAULIC ENGINEERING belongs to one of the largest branches of the national economy — the capital construction of irrigation systems.

Qualified training of hydraulic construction technicians allows graduates to work across the whole range of water management and hydropower. Graduates of the "Hydraulic Engineering" specialty build multi-purpose waterworks, install hydraulic structures, and construct hydropower plants, bridges, pumping stations and water supply systems.
descriptions.five:
Everyone on the planet understands that land is the most priceless wealth. The well-being, economy and ecology of a state depend largely on how people manage land resources.

Today a rational, scientific approach to distributing the country's land resources is a top priority. Graduates of the land management department are prepared to solve land management tasks. They can work in regional, city and district offices of the State Agency for Registration of Rights to Real Estate under the Government of the Kyrgyz Republic, as well as in local self-government bodies. College graduates are also in demand at design and research organizations, private real estate agencies and other organizations dealing with land use.
descriptions.six:
A FISH FARMER works at industrial fish farms, breeding and raising fish in specially equipped ponds, and grows large quantities of fish feed — aquatic plants and animal organisms.

A FISH FARMER organizes and controls the technological process at enterprises that breed and raise young fish, market fish and other aquaculture objects, carries out selection and breeding work, and introduces and monitors fishing rules and the protection of fishery waters from pollution.

A fish farming technician needs the following professional qualities: observation skills, attention, good memory and physical endurance.
descriptions.seven:
Kyrgyzstan is a mountainous republic where a guaranteed harvest in many areas is only possible with reclamation-based farming.

Developing land reclamation to raise crop yields and meet the population's need for food is highly relevant today. This has created the need to train specialists in the republic who can solve practical problems of the efficient use, protection and management of water resources.

Highly efficient use of the country's natural, climatic, land and water resources depends mainly on the qualifications of specialists in land reclamation, rehabilitation and protection.

Graduates of the "Land Reclamation, Rehabilitation and Soil Protection" specialty can apply their broad knowledge in design, construction, repair and operation organizations of the Department of Water Resources and the Ministry of Agriculture of the Kyrgyz Republic, as well as in reclamation, environmental protection and irrigation systems and complexes.
descriptions.eight:
GEODESY is the science of determining the shape and size of the Earth and of measuring the land surface to show it on plans and maps. It is based on two fundamental sciences — mathematics and physics. "Geodesy" is a word of Greek origin meaning "dividing the earth".

Geodesy graduates are ready to work in the construction of industrial and civil buildings and in engineering and geodetic surveys needed to design roads and railways, irrigation networks, settlements, airports, hydraulic structures, power lines and communication lines.

Today a geodesy technician also has a wide field of work in land and urban cadastre and in establishing and fixing the boundaries of territorial units.
descriptions.nine:
INFORMATICS is the fastest-growing field of science and practice of the 21st century. Human civilization has entered a new period — building an information society. In developed countries, 60–70% of the working population is now employed in information processing.

APPLIED INFORMATICS is an unusual specialty. It combines computer science with the areas where computer skills can be applied: economics, management, design, law and much more. In short, an applied informatics specialist is always a "two-in-one" professional. All students of "Applied Informatics" study computer disciplines: informatics and programming, higher mathematics, operating systems, information security and network administration.
descriptions.eleven:
Today the word "ECOLOGY" is used at every level of society — from ordinary citizens to company managers and heads of state.

This is due to the current environmental crisis, when pollution has reached a level that threatens life on a planetary scale.

Graduates of the "Ecology and Environmental Protection" specialty:

— help ensure global and national security through environmental cooperation between all countries of the world;

— carry out mandatory independent environmental assessments of planned, under-construction and operating facilities that are sources of increased danger;

— investigate the causes of natural disasters and develop ways to minimize human impact on nature.

Graduates can work in state environmental protection organizations and in the environmental departments of large enterprises: for example, building any industrial facility always requires an environmental impact assessment.
